source.title: Conductive Collagen-Based Hydrogel Combined With Electrical Stimulation to Promote Neural Stem Cell Proliferation and Differentiation

formulation.evidence: 1 ml of a pyrrole aqueous solution (concentrations of 0 mM, 20 mM, 40 mM, or 60 mM) was mixed with 1 ml of a collagen solution (10 mg/ml)
1 ml of a pyrrole aqueous solution (concentrations of 0 mM, 20 mM, 40 mM, or 60 mM) was mixed with 1 ml of a collagen solution (10 mg/ml)
the mixed solution was soaked in a genipin solution (0.3 wt%)

processing.evidence: The cross-linking treatment was carried out at 37°C for 24 h.

youngs_modulus.evidence: The Young’s moduli of Col/PPy0, Col/PPy20, and Col/PPy40 hydrogels were 654.5 ± 10.32 Pa, 1241.3 ± 20.4 Pa, and 2,684.5 ± 30.2 Pa, respectively

conductivity.evidence: which is 15 times that of Col/PPy0 (0.0038 ± 0.0009 S/cm)

biology.cell_type: neural stem cells from embryonic (E15-16) rat neocortex

culture_days.evidence: seeded on different hydrogels and cultured in the differentiation medium for 3 days

viability_percent.evidence: The highest percentage of viable NSCs was the Col/PPy40 + ES group (91.2 ± 4.8%), followed by Col/PPy40 (80.5 ± 4.7%), and Col/PPy0 (73.5 ± 4.8%) groups

neurite_length.evidence: the shortest neurite length (77.8 ± 19.7 μm) was observed in the Col/PPy0 group

other_outcomes.evidence: The prepared Col/PPy0 hydrogel sample had the fastest degradation rate, and the remaining weight was 36 ± 2.78% on the 28th day.
other_outcomes.name: remaining weight after 28 days in collagenase

other_outcomes.evidence: were significantly higher than those in the Col/PPy40 (3.1 ± 1.0) and Col/PPy0 (2.2 ± 0.9) groups
other_outcomes.name: number of branch points

survival.evidence: The highest percentage of viable NSCs was the Col/PPy40 + ES group (91.2 ± 4.8%), followed by Col/PPy40 (80.5 ± 4.7%), and Col/PPy0 (73.5 ± 4.8%) groups

notes: Degradation in collagenase 1 U/ml at 37°C. Negative control group for viability/neurite studies.
